pr_title: Return error when node info is not found in cache
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

#79076 migrated from using informer's cache to scheduler cache to increase consistency, but there could be race conditions when a node is removed. Note that we have some checks for nil in earlier calls, but nodes can be removed anytime. This could happen more often when doing fast downscales.

This change returns an API error to mimic the behavior in earlier versions.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #89410

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

This is not a problem in 1.17+, because we use a snapshot of the cache, which remains consistent during the scheduling cycle.

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
NONE
```

@xtroncode do you have a cluster where nodes are added/removed frequently?
@ahg-g yes, we use cluster-autoecaler , and scaling activity is frequent.

I think the problem is a consequence of changing listing the nodes from the informer cache to the scheduler cache (which in 1.17 changed again to list from the snapshot): 

In 1.15: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.15/pkg/scheduler/factory/factory.go#L567

In 1.16: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.16/pkg/scheduler/factory/factory.go#L505

[Here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.16/pkg/scheduler/algorithm/priorities/interpod_affinity.go#L186) we check that nodeinfo.Node is not nil, but by the time we get to [L115](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.16/pkg/scheduler/algorithm/priorities/interpod_affinity.go#L186), the node inside nodeInfo gets deleted causing the panic.

in 1.15 this would have caused an error since looking up the node from the informer cache would have returned an error.
The same issue with the inter-pod affinity predicate: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.16/pkg/scheduler/algorithm/predicates/predicates.go#L1307
looking at predicate and priority registry, it seems only interpod affinity uses the node lister, so I think the above two cases are the only ones, but we should double check.

Thanks @xtroncode  for reporting, a fix will soon be patched to 1.16.

Note that 1.17 and above doesn't have this problem because they operate on the snapshot which makes a deep copy of the node object.
Thanks @ahg-g for a quick response in such difficult times. Please let me know if I can help in any way.
